```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

We are using the `cars` data set which gives speed and stopping distance of cars from 1920.


```{r echo=FALSE, fig.align='center', fig.width=5, fig.height=5, fig.cap='Speed versus stopping distance from cars data set'}
fit <- lm(
	dist ~ speed, 
	data = cars
)
plot(cars)
abline(fit)
```

The model is $\beta_0 + \beta_1 \text{Speed} + \epsilon = \text{Stopping Distance}$ where the intercept $\beta_0$ is `r coef(fit)[1]` and $\beta_1$ is `r coef(fit)[2]`.
